public_notes.title: River Homelands And Displacement
public_notes.text: The Tribe describes permanent villages along the Chickahominy River. Its history says the Treaty of 1646 displaced its people to Pamunkey Neck, followed by further settler pressure and a gradual move toward Chickahominy Ridge. It also describes Chickahominy villages as independent of Chief Powhatan while maintaining close ties with neighboring Native peoples. These are the Tribe's historical accounts, not a present land-boundary determination.

public_notes.title: Education And Community Continuity
public_notes.text: The Tribe dates Samaria Indian Baptist Church to 1901 and describes its importance to community life. Its twentieth-century account explains how Virginia's racial policies attacked Native records and restricted education. Community members built schools and funded teachers' salaries; many children went to Oklahoma to finish high school and attend college. The Tribe's published vision connects its future with environmental stewardship and sharing its own story. These are accounts of community persistence and aspirations, not verified program outcomes.

public_notes.title: Education And A Distinct Government
public_notes.text: The Tribe's timeline records a one-room school in New Kent County beginning in 1910. It dates formation of the Eastern Division's own tribal government to 1920 to 1921 and a certificate of incorporation to 1925. It says the school closed in 1950, when students were bused to Samaria Indian School in Charles City County. These dates describe community institutions and a distinct government, not the beginning of the Chickahominy people.

public_notes.title: Food Sovereignty And Dated Plans
public_notes.text: CIT-ED's food-sovereignty page says a 2022 EPA Sustainable Materials Management grant helped develop a community compost and gardening program. The same page describes plans for 2025: a cultural garden for school children and a food forest intended to increase food sovereignty and share knowledge of the land. Those are dated plans in the publisher's account. This source check does not establish whether those plans were completed or what is operating today.
